utu-ḫe₂-ĝal₂: Utuhegal (Langdon ᵈUtu-ĝe-gál, 'Utuḫegal') — the one king of the fifth dynasty of Uruk; the sun-god Utu (UD, with the divine determinative) + ḫe₂-ĝal₂ (GAN, Langdon ĝe, + IG, Langdon gál), ḫe₂-ĝal₂ 'abundance': 'Utu (is) abundance'
ur-{d}namma: Ur-Namma (Langdon Ur-ᵈNammu, after Gadd) — first king of the third dynasty of Ur, father of Shulgi; ur 'man, servant' + the goddess Namma, written with the divine determinative and ENGUR (LAGAB×HAL), 'the deep': 'servant of Namma'
šul-gi: Shulgi (Langdon ᵈDungi, also ᵈDun-gi) — king of Ur (third dynasty), son of Ur-Namma, written with the divine determinative; DUN (read šul, 'young man', Langdon dun) + GI
amar-{d}suen: Amar-Suen (Langdon ᵈBur-ᵈSin) — king of Ur (third dynasty), son of Shulgi, written with the divine determinative; AMAR 'calf' (Langdon's value bur) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin): 'calf of Suen'
i-bi₂-{d}suen: Ibi-Suen (Langdon I-be-ᵈSin, 'Ibe-Sin', in his notes Ibi-Sin) — last king of the third dynasty of Ur, son of Shu-Suen; I + a sign drawn as a box with crossing wedges, taken as NE (read bi₂; Langdon be, i.e. BAD) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU) with the divine determinative; an Akkadian name; the identification of the second sign is uncertain
i₃-si-in: Isin (Langdon Ì-si-in) — city in central Babylonia, seat of the dynasty after Ur; NI (read i₃) + SI + IN, with the place-determinative KI (unread), as i₃-si-in{ki}
iš-bi-er₃-ra: Ishbi-Erra (Langdon Iš-bi-Gir*-ra, 'Ishbi-Girra') — first king of Isin, father of Shu-ilishu; IŠ-BI + a sign that Langdon marks as of uncertain reading (his Gir*), taken here as ARAD read er₃ + RA, the god Erra (Langdon Girra); an Akkadian name; on this prism the god's name has no divine determinative (another copy has it)
šu-i₃-li₂-šu: Shu-ilishu (Langdon ᵈGimil-ì-lí-šu, 'Gimil-ilishu') — king of Isin, son of Ishbi-Erra; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + NI-NI (i₃-li₂, Akkadian ili, genitive of ilum 'god') + ŠU (-šu 'his'): 'the one of his god'; written once with and once without the divine determinative
i-din-{d}da-gan: Idin-Dagan (Langdon I-din-ᵈDa-gan) — king of Isin, son of Shu-ilishu, father of Ishme-Dagan; I-DIN + the god Dagan (DA-GAN, with the divine determinative): Akkadian 'Dagan gave'
iš-me-{d}da-gan: Ishme-Dagan (Langdon Iš-me-ᵈDa-gan) — king of Isin, son of Idin-Dagan; IŠ-ME + the god Dagan (DA-GAN, with the divine determinative): Akkadian 'Dagan heard'
li-bi-it-ašdar: Lipit-Ashdar (Langdon ᵈLi-[bi-it-Ašdar], 'Lipit-Ashdar') — king of Isin, son of Ishme-Dagan; Akkadian lipit 'work of' + Ašdar, Langdon's reading of the name of the goddess Ištar, whose writing is not known from this copy; Langdon prints a divine determinative before the name, but none is drawn on the copy
ur-{d}nin-urta: Ur-Ninurta (Langdon ᵈUr-ᵈNinurta) — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; ur 'man, servant' + the god Ninurta (NIN + IB, read urta): 'servant of Ninurta'; on this prism only {d}ur survives and the god's name is restored by Langdon from another copy
bur-{d}suen: Bur-Suen (Langdon ᵈBur-ᵈSin) — king of Isin, son of Ur-Ninurta, written with the divine determinative (once without it); BUR + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU); on this copy the first sign is drawn as a closed box with inner wedges, unlike the AMAR of the Ur king Amar-Suen whom Langdon also reads Bur-Sin, and is taken here as BUR; that identification is uncertain
li-bi-it-{d}en-lil₂: Lipit-Enlil (Langdon ᵈLi-bi-[it-ᵈ]En-lil, 'Lipit-Enlil') — king of Isin, son of Bur-Suen, written with the divine determinative; LI-BI-IT (it the A₂ sign, restored) + the god Enlil (EN + KID, read lil₂): Akkadian lipit 'work (of)', 'work of Enlil'; Langdon writes his English Lipit
er₃-ra-i-mi-ti: Erra-imiti (Langdon ᵈGir*-ra-i-mi-ti, 'Girra-imiti') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; the god Erra (ARAD read er₃, Langdon's Gir* of uncertain reading, + RA) + I-MI-TI; an Akkadian name; the sense of imiti is not clear
en-lil₂-ba-ni: Enlil-bani (Langdon ᵈEn-lil-ba-ni, 'Enlilbani') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; the god Enlil (EN + KID, read lil₂) + BA-NI, Akkadian bāni 'creator': 'Enlil is creator'
za-am-bi-ia: Zambiya (Langdon ᵈZa-am-bi-i̯a, 'Zambija') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; ZA-AM-BI + IA (i̯a, the sound ya); the sense of the name is not clear
i-ṭe-er-pi₄-ša: Iterpisha (Langdon ᵈI-ṭe-ir-pî-ša, 'Iterpîsha') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; I + DI (ṭe) + IR (er) + KA (read pi₄, Akkadian pû 'mouth') + ŠA; Langdon derives it from eṭir-pî-ša 'her word saves' and notes another writing with KA (Hilprecht's I-te-ir-KA-ša); the identifications of the second and fourth signs are uncertain
ur-du₃-ku₃-ga: Ur-dukuga (Langdon ᵈUr-dù-kug-ga, 'Ur-dukugga') — king of Isin, written with the divine determinative; ur 'man, servant' + a sign Langdon reads dù (taken as KAK, read du₃) + KU₃ 'pure, holy' + GA; the second sign is not certainly identified on the copy and the sense of the name is not clear
suen-ma-gir₂: Suen-magir (Langdon ᵈSin-ma-gir, 'Sin-magir') — king of Isin, the last named on this prism, in whose reign Langdon thinks it was written; the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, with the divine determinative) + MA + a sign taken as GIR₂ (read gir₂; Langdon gir): Akkadian 'Suen is favourable'; the identification of the last sign is uncertain
šu: hand — the ŠU sign; in a scribe's colophon šu X 'by the hand of X', i.e. 'written by X' (Langdon reads it with the Akkadian word, kat, for qāt 'hand of')
nu-ur₂-{d}nin-šubur: Nur-Ninshubur (Langdon Nu-ùr-ᵈNin-subur, 'Nur-Ninsubur') — the scribe who wrote this prism, named in its colophon; NU + UR₂ (Langdon ùr) + the goddess Ninshubur (NIN + ŠUBUR, with the divine determinative): Akkadian nūr 'light (of)', 'light of Ninshubur'

__broaden__.šu-ši: šu-ši — 'sixty', written out as a word (Akkadian šūši) instead of with a numeral sign · after a number of years (mu 7 šu-ši 7 u₄) taken by Langdon as '1/6' (of a year), since he holds that šuš stands for both 60 and 1/6: '7 1/6 years and 7 days'; uncertain
__broaden__.-ma: genitive -a(k) 'of', written -ma after a final m (elam{ki}-ma 'of Elam') · locative -a 'in, at', likewise written -ma after a final m (urim₂{ki}-ma 'in Ur') · also written after urim₂{ki} where no 'of' or 'in' is expected — before the terminative (urim₂{ki}-ma-še₃ 'to Ur') and in the smitten refrain, where other cities stand bare; its function there is not clear
__broaden__.-na: -a(k) 'of' (genitive) written -na after a final n, as in lu₂ kaš-tin-na 'person of kaš-tin'; the analysis is uncertain · locative -a 'in, at' written -na after the final n of a city name (i₃-si-in{ki}-na 'in Isin')
__broaden__.šu-{d}suen: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — name of a king of Akshak (son of Ishu-il; Langdon's restoration, not preserved on this prism) and of a king of Kish; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; where the copy draws the first element in a long form unlike its usual ŠU, the identification is Langdon's and uncertain · also a Gutian king, son of Hablum, the name clear on the prism, the first element again in the long form · also a king of Ur (third dynasty), son of Amar-Suen and father of Ibi-Suen, the first element drawn as the usual compact ŠU
